stem: A rectangular card \(ABCD\) is cut along a straight line from corner \(A\) to a point \(P\) on side \(\overline{DC}\), as shown. The cut makes a \(34^{\circ}\) angle with side \(\overline{AD}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(APC\)?
solution: In right triangle \(ADP\), angle \(D = 90^{\circ}\) and angle \(DAP = 34^{\circ}\), so angle \(APD = 180 - 90 - 34 = 56^{\circ}\).
Angles \(APD\) and \(APC\) form a straight line along \(\overline{DC}\): angle \(APC = 180 - 56 = 124^{\circ}\).
Check: \(\overline{AB} \parallel \overline{DC}\), so angle \(BAP = 90 - 34 = 56^{\circ}\) and angles \(BAP\) and \(APC\) are same-side interior angles that add to \(180^{\circ}\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. 56 is the measure of angle \(APD\); the question asks for the angle on the other side of the cut, \(APC\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(180 - 34\); the \(34^{\circ}\) angle is at \(A\), and it is not the angle next to \(APC\) on line \(DC\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. The angle at \(A\) with side \(\overline{AD}\) is \(34^{\circ}\), but the cut makes a \(56^{\circ}\) angle with the parallel sides, and \(APC\) is obtuse.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['A'][1]==P['B'][1] and P['D'][1]==P['C'][1]==P['P'][1] and P['A'][0]==P['D'][0] and P['B'][0]==P['C'][0]
assert abs(ang('D','A','P')-34)<0.1
ans=180-(180-90-34)
assert abs(ang('A','P','C')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==124
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
